title: Bharata Rules with Rama's Sandals
text:
King Dasharatha of Ayodhya had promised his queen Kaikeyi two wishes. When he prepared to crown his eldest son Rama, she asked that Rama be exiled to the forest for fourteen years and that her own son Bharata be made king instead. Bound by his word, the king agreed, and soon after he died of grief.

Bharata had been away. When he returned and learned what his mother had done, he was horrified. He refused the throne and set out with the army, the royal family and the citizens to find Rama in the forest and bring him back. He found him at Chitrakuta and begged him to return and rule.

Rama refused. He would not break their father's word. When nothing could move him, Bharata asked for Rama's sandals. He carried them back on his head, placed them on the throne, and governed in Rama's name from the village of Nandigrama outside the capital, living simply, dressed like a hermit, and reporting every matter to the sandals as if to the king.

When Rama returned after fourteen years, Bharata handed back the kingdom.
lesson: Sometimes you are given power you did not earn and should not keep. Hold it as a trustee: run things well, take nothing for yourself, and be ready to hand it back.
date: c. 5th century BC to 3rd century AD
